name: 6R migration wave
description: Ingest estate data, classify each workload under one of the six 6R strategies, compute a TCO comparison where relevant, and sequence the workload into a migration wave whose dependencies are respected. Grounded in P20 ("Migration assessment and 6R planning") and evidenced by `agent-assess`, `infracc`, `anytoany` and `cloudshift`.

parameters.name: strategy
parameters.description: The 6R disposition assigned to this workload.

parameters.name: source_ingestion_format
parameters.description: The source estate data format this workload was ingested from.

parameters.name: wave_number
parameters.description: The migration wave this workload is scheduled into.

parameters.name: requires_tco_comparison
parameters.description: Whether a source-vs-target TCO comparison is computed for this workload.

preconditions: The canonical estate model already contains the workload, its resources and dependencies before a strategy is assigned (depends on R0-04's canonical estate model).
A target-provider service-map resolution exists for every resource the workload depends on, or the workload's strategy is retain or retire (P20; spec 7 -- mapping registry).

outputs.description: The 6R disposition recorded against the workload.
Source-vs-target total cost of ownership comparison, when applicable.
The migration wave and its position relative to dependent workloads.
One row in the generated migration roadmap.

validation_rules.description: strategy=retire or strategy=retain must set requires_tco_comparison=false; a workload that is not moving has no destination cost to compare (P20 6R definitions).
wave_number must not schedule a workload earlier than any workload it depends on (spec R2-06: "dependencies respected").
source_ingestion_format=rvtools or hvtools applies only to VMware/ Hyper-V estates; aws_cur or bom_csv applies to AWS estates (`agent-assess` vs `infracc` ingestion).

evidence: CLOUD-ARCHITECTURE-PATTERNS.md P20 ("Ingest estate data (RVTools, HVTools, AWS CUR, BOM, CSV, APIs), classify workloads, map services, apply 6R strategies (rehost, replatform, refactor, repurchase, retire, retain), compute TCO, and produce a roadmap") and `infracc`'s entry ("rehost/replatform/refactor/repurchase/retire/retain model").
